Portable.definition: Runs in a pure-browser sandbox with no local native process. Only the playground family qualifies today: the @verter/wasm compiler host plus the pinned in-browser typescript@6.0.3 worker.

NativeOnly.definition: Requires an explicitly selected local native binary or host process (verter-lsp, verter-tsc, verter-mcp, native flow/semantic solving, project-wide lint and SSR reports).

ExternalOwner.definition: The executing engine is owned outside Verter; Verter pins, provisions, and binds its identity (TypeScript engines under provider modes).

rules: No hidden replacement engine: an execution class is never made true by substituting a different engine.
A browser-executable claim requires the Portable class or (for NativeOnly) shipped browser build evidence; otherwise the claim is rejected (DX0-AC2).
Lapce/Zed WASM launchers stay launchers: they discover and start the native verter-lsp and are NativeOnly, not Portable products.
A Portable product may embed ExternalOwner engines pinned at build time; it may not embed or imply NativeOnly execution.
A class change is a producer-owned port with its own evidence, not an adapter relabel.
Pure-browser and explicit local-native execution are distinct products with distinct receipts.

surfaces.executesWithin: playground.browser (Portable product; typescript@6.0.3 pinned at build time)
